wa_earwax_wall.blurb: Earwax Wall is the far-left end of the Upper Town Wall above the town of Index in the Skykomish Valley. It holds sixteen routes, nearly all of them bolted sport lines, with a pair of trad lines mixed in. The grades start around 5.10, but the bulk sit at 5.12, with a few 5.11s and a couple of 5.13s on top. The rock rewards precise footwork and positive holds on near-vertical to overhanging faces, so it suits strong, experienced sport climbers rather than newcomers. The wall stays partly shaded, which makes it a workable summer choice.

wa_rhinozone.blurb: Rhinozone is a steep little crag near Mazama in the Methow Valley, a short stroll from the Fun Rock parking lot off Lost River Road. Sixteen routes are on record, almost all of them sport with one trad line, and the grades run from 5.7 to 5.11 with the heaviest concentration at 5.10. That spread gives it something for newer leaders stepping up as well as people working harder lines. It sits among a cluster of closely spaced, well-bolted crags, so it pairs easily with a day on the neighbouring walls.

wa_madrone_wall.blurb: Madrone Wall is a small crag on Mount Erie, part of the Orange Area, and it is the wall climbers pass through on the trail down to the lower Orange walls. Its sixteen routes are a mix of sport and trad on faces and slabs, running from an easy 5.2 up to 5.10, though most fall between 5.7 and 5.9. The moderate grades make it popular for climbing classes and for people learning to lead. Expect a short, steep-ish downhill walk with a bit of scrambling to arrive.

wi_union_grove_ridge.blurb: Union Grove Ridge is a small bouldering area in the south part of the Blackhawk Lake Recreation Area. It is made up of a few big, isolated sandstone blocks and some outcrops, with sixteen problems on record. Most are friendly, with about three quarters between V0 and V3, then a handful of harder lines topping out around V8. Sandstone in the surrounding recreation area is a mixed bag, with some solid rock and plenty of loose stuff, so test holds as you go. It is a low-key spot better suited to a quiet session than a big day out.

wi_penokean_wall_the.blurb: The Penokean Wall is a secluded crag tucked into a small wooded valley in the Blue Hills of northern Wisconsin, east of Rice Lake. The main face is roughly 100 feet long and averages about 25 feet tall, so this is a short-route venue. Most of the sixteen listings are top-rope lines, mainly 5.9 to 5.11, with one sport route and a few boulder problems that range from easy to very hard. Most routes face south. It is the most accessible cliff in the Blue Hills, and the valley floor is rocky and scrambly, so wear sturdy shoes.

wi_elephant_rocks.blurb: Elephant Rocks sits on the north end of the East Bluff at Devil's Lake, a short climb up the East Bluff Trail from the North Shore parking. Two buttresses frame an amphitheater between them. Twelve of the sixteen routes are trad and four are top-rope only, covering roughly 5.4 up to 5.12, with the greatest cluster around 5.7. It is considered some of the best roped climbing on the north end, and crack lines are a main feature. Bring gear and the ability to set up your own anchor above.

wi_el_parasol.blurb: El Parasol is a massive boulder with a large, low roof on the West Bluff at Devil's Lake, sitting just above Fat Raccoon, at the left side of the open boulder field. It holds sixteen problems, all bouldering, and the difficulty is steep: a handful of moderate lines starting at V2, then a long run of hard problems in the V9 to V11 range and a couple of true testpieces beyond that. It is an area for strong boulderers looking at the roof, rather than a place for beginners.
